dedupe_keys.name: topo4mec dataset of mobile edge computing network topologies

description: Topo4MEC is a small benchmark dataset of network topologies for mobile edge computing (MEC), where computing servers sit close to mobile base stations. It was published in Data in Brief in 2021 by Bin Xiang, Jocelyne Elias, Fabio Martignon and Elisabetta Di Nitto to give researchers common test cases for placing edge servers, routing traffic and allocating resources. It holds three randomly generated topologies of different sizes and one real-world-based topology for the city of Milan built from 234 LTE cells of the Vodafone network taken from the crowdsourced OpenCelliD database. Each topology lists nodes (base stations and edge sites), links between them with capacities and delays, and the computing capacity of edge servers, and the generation scripts are provided so users can make new instances. Coverage: synthetic networks plus Milan, Italy. Format and access: files and scripts on Zenodo and GitHub, free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: link capacities, delays and server sizes are assumed values, not operator data; the Milan cell list reflects crowdsourced positions from about 2021. Simulation uses: optimisation benchmarks for edge computing placement, network flow tests under node or link failure, and synthetic test systems for digital twins of access networks. Related records: the Telefónica, SEASON and T-Garden reference topologies cover core and metro networks, and OpenCelliD gives cell locations worldwide.
